text:
Aisha: Quick weekly pulse — heads up on a few items we want all leaders to read and act on this week. High level: (1) Private GA readiness, (2) recent latency incident postmortem + mitigations, (3) a small data-retention policy tweak, and (4) Q2 cost target update. Please skim and flag blockers.

Raj: Thanks — can you give an ETA for the canary rollout for the new autoscaler? Customers saw spikes last week and we want to be sure the fix is in prod.

Aisha: Plan is canary tomorrow 9am PT for 10% of traffic, roll to 50% by EOD if metrics look good. Raj, can you own the canary and have SRE on standby? @Ben can you coordinate on alert thresholds? :thumbsup:

Ben: On it. I posted the incident postmortem here: https://internal.redwood/pm/INC-2026-042 — tl;dr root cause was a race in the autoscaler when evicting idle worker groups during a burst. Mitigation deployed (hotfix v2.3.1) removed the race. Action items: add deterministic eviction ordering, add a 30s cool-off before group deletion, and add a load test reproducer.

Maria: For Private GA readiness — Legal confirmed the SOC2 docs and EU DPA language. Still waiting on one security attestation from Partner X; expecting that by Wednesday. Marketing: please don't start GA communications until we get the attestation.

Aisha: Good—marketing hold noted. Maria, can you get the attestation ETA and share in #product by EOD? Also asking PMs to freeze non-critical UI changes for tomorrow's canary window so we reduce churn.

Raj: Quick note on rollbacks: the canary will have an automatic fallback to the previous model variant on error >0.5% or latency > 2s p95. Fallback test script is in infra: 
```
./scripts/canary_fallback_test.sh --retries 3
```
I ran it locally; looks stable.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/autoscaler-v2.3.1 -> group prod-canary-1 at 2026-03-23T09:00:12Z

Ben: If anyone is oncall during the window, monitor these dashboards: /dashboards/latency, /dashboards/autoscaler. I've added temporary alerts for increased tail latency and surge error-rates. I'll be available on the bridge.

Aisha: Incident summary for execs (one-paragraph to forward if needed): "We saw a production latency spike impacting a subset of dedicated customers due to an autoscaler race condition during a burst. Hotfix v2.3.1 mitigated the immediate issue; long-term fixes include deterministic eviction ordering and a canary-controlled rollout. No customer data was exposed. We will follow up with individual customer outreach where SLA windows were missed." Please share with customer-success leads as needed.

Maria: Also: policy tweak — short change to data-retention defaults for Hosted API logs: retention reduced from 90 -> 60 days for non-PII debug logs to cut storage costs. Security sign-off complete. We'll publish the update in the docs and add a banner in Console.

Aisha: Cost target update: finance and infra are projecting a 7% unit-cost reduction from batching and cache improvements; we still need another 3% to hit the Q2 objective. Ops, please prioritize the caching tickets flagged in the Optimize backlog.

Raj: Will deprioritize one lower-value perf experiment and move two caching PRs to the front of the queue.

Ben: Postmortem follow-ups are in JIRA (INC-2026-042). I'll own the remediation checklist; will update status daily in #eng-oncall until closed.

Aisha: Thanks team. Owners: Raj (canary + rollback), Ben (alerts + postmortem), Maria (attestation + comms), Finance/Infra (costs). I'll check back Friday with a short readout. If anything goes sideways during the canary, ping me directly. :eyes:

Raj: Copy that.

Maria: Will update Marketing and CS after attestation.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: canary/autoscaler-v2.3.1 -> group prod-canary-1 succeeded at 2026-03-23T09:05:00Z

Ben: Canary monitoring green at +30m. No elevated latency signals and fallback not triggered.

Aisha: Great — keeping the team focused. Small ask: keep comms short and clear if we need to escalate to customers. Appreciate the rapid responses. :sparkles:
